source_lines.29: In a finite DAG, a **route** is a finite sequence of vertices with consecutive vertices adjacent by an arrow in either direction; repeated vertices are allowed. Collider and noncollider status is assigned to each internal occurrence using its two incident route arrows. A route is **active given $C$** if each noncollider occurrence is outside $C$ and each collider occurrence is an ancestor of $C$, including membership in $C$. If an active route joins vertices $x,y\notin C$ with $x\ne y$, then an active distinct-vertex path joins $x$ and $y$ given $C$.
source_lines.41: 1.1 Among active routes with these endpoints choose one of minimum length. If a repeated vertex occurs at an endpoint, discard the initial segment through the later occurrence of $x$, or the terminal segment from the earlier occurrence of $y$. Endpoints are outside $C$, and all retained internal occurrences have their old incidences, so the shortened route is active. Consequently any repetition in a minimum route consists of two internal occurrences of a vertex $v$. Delete the segment between two such occurrences and identify them. Only the two incidences at the joined occurrence of $v$ change. If $v\in C$, its old occurrences were both colliders, so the joined occurrence is still a collider. If $v\notin C$ and the joined occurrence is a noncollider, it is allowed; if it is a collider and $v$ is an ancestor of $C$, it is also allowed. [given, F1, choose, construct]
source_lines.43: 2.1 The sole remaining possibility is that the join makes $v$ a collider although $v$ is not an ancestor of $C$. Both original occurrences were then noncolliders. The retained edge before the first occurrence points into $v$, so its deleted departure edge must point out of $v$; likewise the deleted arrival edge at the second occurrence points out of $v$, since its retained departure edge points into $v$. Traverse the deleted segment starting with its arrow out of $v$. There must be a first place where its arrows cease to point forward: the final arrow points backward, and an entirely forward return to $v$ would also contradict acyclicity. At that first change is a collider $w$, reached from $v$ by a directed segment. A directed segment in a DAG has no repetitions. Activity of the original route makes $w$ an ancestor of $C$, hence $v$ an ancestor of $C$, a contradiction. Thus every loop deletion above is active and strictly shorter, contradicting minimality. The minimum route is therefore a path. [F1, step 1.1, construct] ∎

source_lines.58: 1.1 Suppose an active path joins $X$ to $Y$. From any noncollider follow an outgoing path edge forward until reaching an endpoint or a collider. The reached endpoint is in $X\cup Y$, while a reached collider is an ancestor of $C$ by activity. Thus every path vertex is in $H=\operatorname{An}_G(X\cup Y\cup C)$. Replace each collider segment $u\to w\leftarrow v$ by its moral edge $u-v$; colliders cannot be consecutive along a path. The resulting walk avoids $C$, since all retained internal vertices were noncolliders and the endpoints are outside $C$. Loop deletion in this undirected graph yields a moral path avoiding $C$. [F1, F2, construct]
source_lines.60: 1.2 Conversely suppose a moral path avoiding $C$ joins $X$ to $Y$. Keep its skeleton edges, and expand each remaining moral edge $u-v$ using a common child $w\in H$ as $u\to w\leftarrow v$. This is a finite route; its inserted occurrences are colliders and all its other occurrences are outside $C$. Every collider is in $H$. Call a collider occurrence bad if its vertex is not an ancestor of $C$. Among routes joining $X$ to $Y$ with every vertex in $H$ and every noncollider outside $C$, minimize the number of bad collider occurrences; the expanded route makes the class nonempty. If $w$ is a bad occurrence, it is an ancestor of some $s\in X\cup Y$. A directed path from $w$ to $s$ avoids $C$, since otherwise $w$ would be an ancestor of $C$. If $s\in X$, replace the whole prefix up to this occurrence of $w$ by that directed path traversed backward; if $s\in Y$, replace the suffix by the path traversed forward. If $w=s$, simply terminate at that occurrence. Otherwise the retained incident arrow points into $w$ and the new incident arrow points out of $w$, making it an allowed noncollider. All new internal chain occurrences are noncolliders outside $C$, and other retained occurrences have their original incidences. Intersections of the chain with the retained segment cause repetitions only; no loops are deleted in this step, and activity is defined occurrence by occurrence. At least the selected bad occurrence disappears and no new bad occurrence is introduced, contradicting minimality. Thus the minimum route is active. Its endpoints are distinct because $X,Y$ are disjoint, and [F3] gives an active path with those endpoints. [F1, F2, F3, construct, choose]
